thread:
maya: Heads-up — rolled a small shadow of rerank-q3-int4 (rerank model, long-doc suite) into staging last night. Latency ~25% down, cost -30%, but MRR on long-doc slice is -1.8%.
sam: Can you paste the A/B slice numbers? how big is the slice?
maya: Shadow was ~5k requests sampled over 6 hours, weighted toward long-docs (docs > 3k tokens). Quick snapshot: baseline MRR=0.412, rerank-q3=0.404, p=0.02 on that slice. Overall product-level MRR unchanged.
jordan: Hmm 1.8% absolute relative? that's borderline. What are our rollback heuristics currently for rerank models?
evan: Current canary policy: auto-fallback if any key-quality metric drops >2% relative AND p<0.01 OR if absolute drop >0.03. But that was tuned for shortform, long-doc is noisier.
maya: Right — long-doc variance higher. I think we need a slice-aware threshold, otherwise we keep oscillating.
sam: Agreed. Proposal: use a combined rule — require both relative drop >2% AND effect size >0.2 (Cohen's d) OR sustained drift over 3 windows. Also increase p-value cutoff to 0.005 for small samples? Not sure.
jordan: I'd prefer metric delta + KL/entropy signal. If rerank changes distribution (e.g., avg pairwise score delta) we should be more cautious.
evan: We have entropies: avg score entropy reduced by 8% (tighter distribution) on rerank-q3. That could explain MRR dip for long docs where more nuanced scoring helps.
maya: What's the cost tradeoff? If cost reduction is 30% and user-level metrics unchanged, maybe acceptable for many customers, but long-doc users are sensitive.
sam: For Hosted we could route long-doc traffic to baseline for now. Canary config idea:
```
canary:
  duration: 24h
  sample: 5% global
  slices:
    - name: long-doc
      match: "tokens>3000"
      traffic: 0% (initial)
  auto-fallback:
    metric: long-doc-MRR
    relative_threshold: 0.015
    pvalue: 0.01
    windows: 3
```
We'd start at 0% long-doc and do a slow tilt to 5% if stable.
jordan: That looks reasonable. Also add an entropy monitor: rollback if score-entropy decreases >10% AND MRR drop >1% across slice.
evan: I'll add it to the canary engine rule set. Implementation note: entropy calc is per-session avg pairwise score entropy; we already have a streaming metric.
maya: Action items: evan to update canary policy + deploy config, sam to run a targeted A/B with long-doc routing (baseline vs rerank-q3) for 48h at 10% traffic, jordan to prepare eval prompts for long-doc re-ranking edge cases. I'll file a runbook note.
sam: I'll also add a cost-policy tag so Sales/Customer Success can opt-in to rerank-q3 for cost-sensitive customers.
maya: Good. If the A/B shows persistent >1.5% MRR regression on long-doc but overall cost wins, we'll gate via routing rules (long-doc -> baseline). Otherwise we promote.
deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: canary-rerank-q3-config v2 will be deployed to staging canary at 2026-03-21T14:20Z (jobs queued). :gear:
reliability-bot: Alert rule created: `rerank_q3_longdoc_mrr_drop` — fires if relative drop >1.5% for 2 consecutive 1h windows.
maya: Thanks all — will monitor dashboards and reconvene after 24h of the A/B. :eyes:
